This tutorial uses the supplied two-page Quarto project in `examples/minimal`.
Its material is fictional. You will render ordinary pages, inspect a graph of
explicit public declarations, change a label and optionally explore the diagram.
You need QMD/YAML authoring and normal Quarto commands, not Node, npm or an
author-written JavaScript file.

This tutorial describes the local 0.0.16 development candidate. The README
distinguishes current checks from earlier regression and native/browser evidence
on Windows with Quarto 1.11.5 pre-release. Use its support boundaries when
evaluating another version or environment.

You can render this `example.qmd` as a readable instruction page. **Rendering
this instruction page does not run graph extraction.** Extraction is a
project-level workflow: the exercise below runs inside the existing minimal
project with its `_quarto.yml`, `knowledge.yml` and native source pages.

## 1. Open the supplied project and install

Start in this repository's root folder. Keep the distributed `examples/minimal`
files together; the declarations refer to their current filenames and anchors.
The local-source installation selects the matching local candidate:

```powershell
cd examples/minimal
quarto add ../.. --no-prompt
```

The sample `_quarto.yml` already selects the unqualified
`knowledge-graph-extraction` filter used by that local installation. Installing
from GitHub in your own project instead uses the owner-qualified selector
documented in the README. Do not add duplicate lifecycle hooks: installation
contributes the prepare/finalise hooks automatically.

## 2. Render your first graph

While still in `examples/minimal`, use your editor's **Render Project** command
or run:

```powershell
quarto render
```

Open `_site/index.html` and follow **Read the source-linked knowledge graph
report**. The report is at `_site/knowledge-graph/report.html`.

You should see the mathematical and educational meanings of **action** as
different records, with their own identities, domains and source links. The
mathematical definition occurs on both pages through a native Quarto include.
Its identity is shared while its containing-page destinations differ. The
theorem, proof and fictional citation remain ordinary Quarto content.

No word matching creates those identities. The catalogue explicitly declares
them. Records in this synthetic file marked `public: false` do not enter the
graph; this does not hide ordinary authored page content or HTML attributes.

## 3. Make a small YAML edit

Open `knowledge.yml`. Find the object with `id: math:group-action` and change
its English label from `action` to `group action`. Keep its identifier,
`scope`, source path and anchor unchanged. Render again:

```powershell
quarto render
```

The report should now show **group action** for that mathematical object and
retain **action** for the educational object. The mathematical identifier and
its source links should remain the same. The private graph cache is derived
data: you do not need to edit it or run a separate graph build.

Next, edit a sentence in `index.qmd` and render again. QMD owns your page's
content; the YAML catalogue owns its declared semantic identities and graph
relationships. The `_definition.qmd` file demonstrates native content reuse.

## 4. Turn on the interactive view

In the sample `_quarto.yml`, add `navigation: true` to its existing complete
`knowledge-graph` mapping:

```yaml
knowledge-graph:
  declarations: knowledge.yml
  mode: update
  navigation: true
```

Run a normal preview from this same project folder:

```powershell
quarto preview --render all
```

Follow the graph report's **Explore the graph** link. Use the HTTP preview for
the module-based navigator; opening its HTML through `file:` can block loading.
The static report remains available independently of the diagram.

Try dragging a node, then release it. An active layout resumes arranging it;
an explicit pause or reduced-motion preference takes priority. Use the search,
textual source list, movement buttons and full-page controls as alternatives
to dragging. Layout position is not an additional relationship or evidence.

To follow a reading journey, use **A route through these records**. Choose the
educational **action** as Start and the mathematical **group action** as Goal,
then **Compute a bounded candidate**. Inspect its direction, cost and source
scope before choosing **Accept this route explicitly**. Following a source link
now continues in the same tab, with a **Your reading route** panel on the source
page. Use that panel to explore another concept and return, or mark the current
concept complete and continue. Merely visiting its page does not mark it known.
**Return to graph navigator** keeps the accepted route and its return context.

Reading continuity is enabled with navigation; no extra YAML or script is
required for this exercise. Retention is normally session-only. Choose the
explicit retention checkbox only if you want it kept in this browser after the
session, and use **Forget reading route** to remove it. The README explains
storage failures and changed snapshots. Ordinary new-tab browser controls
remain available.

If you also activate other companion extensions on the tested Windows Quarto
prerelease, consult the README's preview compatibility notes before relying on
aggregate graph coverage. The sample exercise itself does not need a custom
server or author script.

## 5. Optional: connect two graph views with QMD and YAML

Keep the same project. This exercise adds a view and a deliberate comparison;
it does not equate the two meanings of *action*.

In `knowledge.yml`, add this top-level mapping alongside `objects` and
`relations`:

```yaml
graphs:
  mathematics:
    label: Mathematics
    navigation: true
    search: true
```

Find the existing `math:group-action` object. Add these two fields to that
object, keeping its other fields and its identifier unchanged:

```yaml
graph: website
graphs: [website, mathematics]
```

There is still one author declaration. It now appears in the website view and
the named mathematics view. Other objects keep their existing website membership.

Add an ordinary identified section at the end of `education.qmd`:

```markdown
## Compare two uses of action {#action-comparison}

Educational action and a mathematical group action are different concepts.
This reading route lets us contrast them without treating them as synonyms.
```

Then add this **top-level** section to `knowledge.yml`:

```yaml
navigation-links:
  - id: he:compare-actions
    from: {graph: website, id: he:action}
    to: {graph: mathematics, id: math:group-action}
    public: true
    weight: 1
    source: {path: education.qmd, anchor: action-comparison}
```

Finally, extend the existing complete `_quarto.yml` mapping:

```yaml
knowledge-graph:
  declarations: knowledge.yml
  mode: update
  navigation: true
  federation:
    graphs: [website, mathematics]
    label: Compare the two domains
```

Render the full project and refresh the HTTP preview. The expected graph report
lists the separate website and mathematics navigators plus **Compare the two
domains**, the connected view. Its reading routes use the explicit public link
and retain the original graph identities. A declared link whose freshly rendered
source lacks its anchor fails the build; correct the anchor and render again.
Unavailable endpoints, unobserved link sources or unresolved prerequisites
withhold that connected navigator rather than inventing a complete route.

Open native website search and enter `action`. **All content** keeps the native
search experience. **Search within → Mathematics** narrows discovery to that
graph; **Website pages only** returns the original page index. If the optional
filter is unavailable, ordinary All content search remains usable. None of
these actions needs a model download.

## 6. Use the approach in an existing website

Keep your own `_quarto.yml`, theme, navigation and source pages. Add the installed
filter to its existing `filters` list instead of replacing that configuration.

The author files in this exercise are `knowledge.yml`, `index.qmd`,
`education.qmd`, `_definition.qmd` and `references.bib`. An existing website
does not need to copy every demonstration file. Start by copying/adapting the
catalogue as a new project-root `knowledge.yml` and pointing its declarations
to your own QMD paths and native anchors. Remove demonstration records and
occurrences unless you also retain their source pages. Do not overwrite an
existing catalogue or `index.qmd`; add reviewed entries to your existing files.
The smaller `knowledge-compact.yml` is an alternative reference for the same
scoped-declaration pattern.

Keep private review data and `.quarto/knowledge-graph` out of website resources.
Use the default deterministic workflow first; optional AI assistance is a
separate authoring choice and does not run during rendering.

## 7. Choose your next step

Return to the repository root with `cd ../..`. The [README](README.md#declarations-and-configuration) is the advanced
reference for named graphs, custom schemas, navigator preferences, public
exports, incremental reuse, reviewed frozen baselines and private authoring/AI
commands.

Use its [named-question profiles](README.md#offer-named-questions-without-author-javascript)
for your own hierarchy/evidence/date schema,
[topic fragments](README.md#publish-optional-topic-fragments) for progressive
navigator detail loading, [public data packaging](README.md#package-the-public-data-for-reuse)
for declared rights and export hashes,
[contextual review](README.md#review-ambiguous-terminology-without-a-model) for
private proposals about existing identities, and
[private history commands](README.md#inspect-retained-history-privately)
to inspect receipt-bound older snapshots without republishing them. These are
optional next steps; the normal author loop remains edit QMD/YAML, render, preview.

For your own ordinary activity pages, the
[reading continuity settings](README.md#continue-a-route-through-the-source-pages)
add labelled local detours. They do not provide a live Argumentation Sandbox
proof roundtrip. The normal tutorial needs neither a model nor a data licence
decision; packaging and AI authoring remain separate opt-in choices.

When Interactive CV and this extension are activated together, the CV's eligible
public catalogue supplies its own separate graph automatically. Do not recreate
CV records in `knowledge.yml`. Other compatible companions can consume the
same explicit public identities; installing them alone does not activate their
filters or imply consent to model downloads.

Native includes keep their containing-page links. If you want to expose which
original include contains a literal anchor token, the README's
[source-origin option](README.md#original-source-coordinates)
requires explicit public source paths and leaves ambiguous tokens unavailable.
Unambiguous heading sections and fenced definitions/proofs also retain their
original structural bounds and hashes; included files stay separate origins.
To propose relationships between existing identities after rendering, follow the
[private relation review](README.md#propose-and-review-relations). This optional
step keeps review separate from the normal edit, render and preview loop.
If literal context cues are insufficient, the README's
[semantic identity proposals](README.md#propose-semantic-identities-using-a-local-model)
use an explicitly started local model. That advanced workflow keeps server
configuration, prompts, responses and review files in a separate private folder
outside the project and every Git checkout. Put only already-public text in QMD;
no model is needed for this tutorial.
For a custom client, the [query-provider contract](README.md#discover-the-public-query-provider)
describes the current public graph and shared query API; the normal tutorial
needs no client code or additional setting.
